clue.text: Knave (Spade, say) squeezed in top event

indicators.note: spade-and-say has the word for top pressed into its middle, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: S is the card abbreviation for spades
EG, for example, is what 'say' means
a cap is a top or lid
a race is a sporting event

explanation.surface: The knave of spades is slipped into the deck at the key moment of a card contest.
explanation.walkthrough: The parenthesis makes you picture the knave of spades as a card, but the knave is the definition, in its old sense of a rogue, and the spade only gives its card-suit abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A scamp or rascal is a knave in the old sense of a rogue, a young ne'er-do-well.

clue.text: Peter, rail employee, offers a precaution

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
a guard works on a train

explanation.surface: A railwayman named Peter suggests a sensible precaution.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter looks like a man's name; in thieves' slang a peter is a safe, a convention worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: A protective measure taken in advance is a precaution.

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows, so 'of' marks a concealed answer

explanation.surface: A note on a Greek deity, especially as god of war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' points into 'war, especially', where the god sits across the two words; the clue doubles as a description of him.
explanation.definitionFit: The Olympian deity of battle in Greek myth, the counterpart of Roman Mars.

indicators.note: the rector's letter comes in the course of the recesses word, so it sits inside it

parts.note: niches are recesses in a wall

explanation.surface: An English clergyman decorates church alcoves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' puts R inside NICHES, after the opening N, and E for English goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To adorn or improve something is to decorate it, making it richer in appearance.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Composer joins party, (5)' is cut short after the comma: RAVE + L needs a word giving L that is missing, and a search of the exact text finds nothing.

indicators.note: the Henry letter is hemmed in by the conveyor word, so it is placed inside it

parts.note: a carter conveys goods by cart
H is the symbol for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry finds himself bound by the haulier's agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricted by' puts H inside CARTER, after the C.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal written grant or agreement, such as a hire deal for a boat or plane, is a contract.

clue.text: Old copper in temper, reportedly, after set-to?

indicators.note: the temper piece comes after the set-to piece in the answer

parts.note: a scrap is a fight or set-to

indicators.note: signals that the word for temper is heard rather than written

parts.note: mettle is temper or spirit

explanation.surface: A policeman loses his temper after a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old copper' suggests a retired policeman; it is discarded copper sent for recycling. The homophone works because the two words for spirit and for iron or tin are said alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Discarded copper is an example of waste material salvaged for melting down.

definitions.meaning: a headlong dash, as in going at full tilt
a profession or line of work

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a headlong charge and a lifelong occupation.

clue.text: Master of the Rolls? Yes and no

definitions.text: Master of the Rolls? Yes and no

parts.words: Master of the Rolls? Yes and no
parts.note: the title of a senior English judge, read instead as someone in charge of a Rolls-Royce car, which is so in one sense and not in the other

explanation.surface: Is someone a senior judge or not?
explanation.walkthrough: The Master of the Rolls is a senior judge in England; here the Rolls is a Rolls-Royce car, controlled by the person paid to drive it.
explanation.definitionFit: A paid driver of a luxury car controls the Rolls but holds no judicial title.

clue.text: Vessel's left, on the way to

parts.note: via means by way of, passing through on the way to somewhere

explanation.surface: A ship has departed and is en route somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' and 'left' suggest a ship sailing; the vessel is a small bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A small glass bottle for medicine is a container, a vessel in the general sense.

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of geneva are mixed up

explanation.surface: Fetch a gin cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: Geneva is an old name for gin, which makes 'cocktail' look like a drink; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact revenge is to get back at, or get even with, someone.

clue.text: A right chiseller, this one literal

definitions.text: A right chiseller, this one literal

parts.words: A right chiseller, this one literal
parts.note: a chiseller is slang for a swindler, but this one works with a real chisel, carving stone or wood

explanation.surface: A real cheat, and this one means it literally.
explanation.walkthrough: Chiseller is slang for a cheat; taken literally it is someone who uses a chisel on stone or wood.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist who carves statues uses a chisel, so is literally a chiseller.

parts.note: regimen is an old word for a system of government
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A government is structured, according to a note from the Democrats.
explanation.walkthrough: REGIMEN, a rule or system of government, is the old sense; REGIME is a trap that leaves the letters short.
explanation.definitionFit: Strictly ordered and disciplined, like a military unit, means organised.

clue.text: Corporal gets the message, accepting tip from sergeant

indicators.note: the message word takes in the sergeant's tip, so it goes inside

parts.note: a moral is the message of a story

indicators.note: the tip here is the final letter at the end of the word sergeant

explanation.surface: An army corporal receives a message that includes something from his sergeant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporal' looks like a rank; it is the adjective meaning bodily. 'tip from' takes the T at the end of sergeant, not the S, and 'accepting' puts it inside MORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Bodily, of the flesh, means subject to death as human bodies are.

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A dandy orders beer in a cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vault' and 'Lager' suggest a beer cellar; the vault is a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumping over a stooping person is a kind of vaulting leap in a children's game.

parts.note: a person of great importance, read as someone with a very big bank account

explanation.surface: Someone of great importance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of great account' usually means important; here the account is a bank balance.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose power comes from wealth has a large bank balance.

indicators.note: the instruments word takes the former word captive inside it

parts.note: drums are musical instruments
old means former, as in an old flame

explanation.surface: Percussion that takes in some old blues music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blues' and 'Instruments' together suggest music; the blues here are low spirits, a sense the surface hides.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in low spirits, the blues, is a state of gloom and inactivity.

clue.text: Cross region and back with access to stage

indicators.note: the two pieces together are read from the end to the start

parts.note: a rood is a cross, especially in a church
a part is a region, as in parts of the country

explanation.surface: Cross a region and return, with a way onto the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ROOD and PART together, giving TRAPDOOR; 'Cross' looks like a verb but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged flap in the theatre floor lets actors appear on the boards from below.

clue.text: A hint of termites in whole floor

indicators.note: the termite letter is put inside the whole word

parts.note: sound means whole and undamaged

indicators.note: only a hint, the first letter, of termites is used

explanation.surface: Signs of termites throughout a whole floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'floor' is a verb here, meaning to amaze. 'hint of' gives T, and 'in' puts it inside SOUND after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: To floor someone is to stun or amaze them completely.

indicators.note: the employment word sits inside the quiet word

parts.note: mum means silent, as in keep mum
use is employment, putting to use

explanation.surface: A job in a quiet gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: Mum for quiet comes from the British phrase 'keep mum', meaning say nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A building displaying collections to the public is a centre for exhibitions.

clue.text: Using dash of eloquence, spar with wit

indicators.note: only a dash, the opening letter, of eloquence is used

parts.note: a sprit is a spar on a sailing boat

explanation.surface: Using a little eloquence, someone spars verbally with wit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spar' suggests verbal sparring; it is a ship's pole, the SPRIT, after E from 'dash of eloquence'.
explanation.definitionFit: A French borrowing for liveliness of mind and quick humour.

definitions.meaning: a line of geographical position measured north or south of the equator
freedom of movement, slack, as in play in a rope

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a parallel on the map and freedom of action.

definitions.meaning: a verb, to follow or track someone

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a track to follow and to follow someone closely.

parts.note: a coup is a successful stroke or stratagem
on means forward, advanced

explanation.surface: A clever move is made forward in soldiers' lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'billet' suggests soldiers' lodging; here it is a ticket or voucher, an older sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A billet can be a ticket or note, and a voucher is a detachable ticket.

indicators.note: the plant is denied, meaning deprived of, the sun letter

parts.note: sedge is a grassy plant of wet ground

explanation.surface: A plant in the flower border gets no sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Border plant' reads as a garden plant, but 'Border' is the definition and 'plant' the sedge.
explanation.definitionFit: A rim or margin is a border.

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the pieces read backwards

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast or faddist, as in a health nut

explanation.surface: A food faddist turns down fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns A NUT round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A large ocean food fish, a kind of mackerel.

parts.note: under means lower or inferior
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A reversal of fortune for the weaker team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverse' looks like a verb; it is a noun, the back or lower face of something.
explanation.definitionFit: The reverse of a coin or object is its bottom or hidden face.

clue.text: A cash allowance is included for youth

indicators.note: the allowance piece is included inside the other pieces

parts.note: a cent is a coin, a piece of cash
dole's, short for dole is, the dole being a state allowance

explanation.surface: A cash allowance is included for young people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'allowance is' is read as the contraction of 'dole is', the dole being British unemployment benefit, so the apostrophe-S counts as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is a young person, a youth.
